simple.meaning: תִּרְשָׁתָא (Tirshâthâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “the title of a Persian deputy or governor.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תִּרְשָׁתָא (H8660) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 2:63, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תִּרְשָׁתָא (H8660) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in תִּרְשָׁתָא (H8660) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: תִּרְשָׁתָא (Tirshâthâʼ) / H8660 is traced through Ezra 2:63, Nehemiah 7:65, Nehemiah 7:69, Nehemiah 8:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: the title of a Persian deputy or governor
definitions.full: H8660. tirshatha תִּרְשָׁתָא noun masculine Tirshathâ, title of Persian governor in Judaea , according to Mey Entstehung d. Jud. 194 and others = His Excellency (read Tarshathâ ) otherwise Lag Symm. i. 60 (compare Arm. Stud. §§ 280, 1680) . — As Mey l.c. , Scheft 93f. ( tarsvta , the feared, revered ) Moss Hast. DB TIRSHATHA Che Ency. Bib. ID .; — ׳הַתּ Ezra 2:63 = Neh 7:65 , 69 (Baer Gi; 7:70 van d. H.); of Nehemiah 8:9 ; 10:1 .

occurrences.englishText: The governor told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.
The governor told that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to minister with Urim and Thummim.
their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.

Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people, said to all the people, “Today is holy to Yahweh your God. Don’t mourn, nor weep.” For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law.
